goal: Create the query/ module from scratch -- crates/monokl/src/query/mod.rs, lexer.rs, parser.rs, and plan.rs -- implementing monokl's query language exactly per docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md:643-897: a hand-written Lexer (Token enum, zero-derive Lexer<'a> struct, 2 pub + 6 private methods), a recursive-style parser (Modifier, ParsedTerm, parse(), content_to_term()) with an exact, traced token-dispatch order including the documented "+regex:foo" degradation, and a QueryPlan that partitions parsed terms into required/excluded/scored index vectors and exposes search_patterns(). lib.rs already declares `pub mod query;` unconditionally (verified, no changes needed there) -- this plan's 19 tasks bring that declaration's target into existence, file by file, criterion by criterion.
architecture:
query/ does not exist on disk yet; this is the first plan to create it, not extend an existing shared file the way SPEC-003/005/006/007/008's plans extended types.rs/tests_types.rs. Unlike those five prior tracks -- pure derive/attribute struct-and-enum declarations with no hand-written function bodies -- this spec is dominated by real algorithmic control flow (a lexer's character-by-character dispatch, a parser's multi-token lookahead, an escape-sequence state machine), so this plan follows a genuinely different rigor allocation: structural pins (scoped diff of derive lists/field order, matching the established SPEC-003 through SPEC-008 convention) are used only for the 6 criteria that are pure shape claims (AC-001, AC-002, AC-003, AC-008, AC-016, AC-021); the remaining 16 criteria are proven with real, hand-traced runtime assertions exercising every dispatch branch, escape case, and boundary condition the spec names -- byte-consumption counts via direct access to Lexer's private `pos` field (legal from an inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block, since it is a descendant module of `lexer` and Rust's privacy model grants descendant modules access to private items), the 4 concrete read_quoted() escape examples traced character-by-character, the NBSP/Unicode-vs-ASCII-whitespace distinction, the LIMIT=64 boundary at exactly 64 and 65 terms, and the two flagship swallowed-lookahead-token traces ("regex: -foo" in T-011, "+regex:foo"/"-regex:foo" in T-012, and a third independently-discovered instance of the identical pattern for "+ +foo" in T-009 -- not named by any spec criterion directly, but a direct, verified consequence of AC-010's own wildcard-arm claim, caught only by writing the test and observing real output diverge from a plausible-but-wrong initial assumption during this plan's own drafting).

Tests are inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }` blocks within each of lexer.rs/parser.rs/plan.rs -- NOT a shared tests_types.rs-style file -- per this project's own more-idiomatic-for-a-non-shared-module convention, and because query/ is used by no other spec in this project, so there is no shared-file contention hazard to guard against here (the exact hazard class that cost PLAN-003/005/006/007/008 real gate rounds on tests_types.rs). This also means every task in this plan uses a WHOLE-FILE `cat > file` rewrite, never `cat >>` append -- appending a bare `#[test] fn` to the end of a file that already ends in a `mod tests { ... }` closing brace would land the new test OUTSIDE that module, breaking the intended single-mod-per-file grouping; a whole-file rewrite keeps the closing brace always correctly placed and is safe here specifically because these files are exclusive to this spec.

Every task was built and proven empirically before this plan was written: each of the 19 cumulative file states below was written into a real isolated /tmp fixture crate (mirroring src/lib.rs + src/error.rs + src/query/*.rs, avoiding the pre-existing io-errors/orin-cargo registry gap that blocks a literal `cargo build` against the real crates/monokl manifest -- same isolation pattern PLAN-001/003/004/005/006/007/008 established) and run through real `cargo test` against cargo 1.96.0, confirming both that every intermediate state compiles standalone (query/mod.rs never declares a submodule before that submodule's file exists -- lexer.rs alone in T-001-T-006, +parser.rs from T-007, +plan.rs from T-015) and the exact cumulative passing-test count after every single task: 15 -> 21 -> 24 -> 26 -> 29 -> 31 (T-001 through T-006, lexer.rs) -> 32 -> 35 -> 40 -> 41 -> 45 -> 47 -> 49 -> 50 (T-007 through T-014, parser.rs) -> 54 -> 55 -> 56 -> 58 -> 59 (T-015 through T-019, plan.rs + mod.rs) -- 13 of which are error.rs's own already-gated SPEC-001 tests (present in every fixture snapshot as a constant baseline), the rest newly added by this plan's own tasks. One test's initial expectation was corrected during this empirical build: T-009's "+ +foo" case was first assumed to produce a Required term (naive reading: "the second + becomes its own Plus token"), but real `cargo test` output showed Optional instead -- tracing the actual control flow confirmed the second '+' is consumed as the FIRST Plus's lookahead content (a bare Token::Plus, content_to_term's wildcard arm -> None), never reaching the main loop as its own token; this is documented in T-009's own step text now, not silently corrected.

No append-only discipline is therefore needed here (unlike types.rs/tests_types.rs, touched by five plans in sequence) -- every task in this plan safely uses a whole-file `cat > file` rewrite. crates/monokl/src/lib.rs itself needs NO edit for this plan: verified by reading the current file directly (line 21, `pub mod query;`, no `#[cfg(feature = ...)]` gate above it, positioned alphabetically among the other unconditional `pub mod` declarations) -- the declaration this plan's files fulfill already exists and is already correct; this plan only needs to make the module tree underneath it exist on disk. Future plans building tokens.rs (Track 7 per .claude/plans/ACTIVE.md) or text_search.rs/rank/ (Tracks 8-9) will import QueryPlan/parse/Modifier/ParsedTerm from `crate::query::{...}` (per this plan's T-015 mod.rs re-export surface) but will not need to modify query/mod.rs, lexer.rs, parser.rs, or plan.rs themselves.
reasoning: Central departure from SPEC-003 through SPEC-008's planning discipline, worked through before writing any task: those five specs' plans all extended a shared, already-existing file (types.rs/tests_types.rs) with pure derive/attribute declarations, so their per-task rigor centered on scoped-diff structural pins (exact derive lists, field/variant declaration order) proven via grep/diff against source text -- no hand-written function body existed anywhere in those five specs' own scope for a test to exercise behaviorally. SPEC-009 is the first track in this project with real, hand-written control flow (a lexer's dispatch, a parser's lookahead, an escape state machine), so applying the SAME structural-pin-only technique here would leave 16 of 22 criteria's actual behavioral claims completely unverified -- the criteria themselves are worded as exact input-to-output traces ("for the specific input '+regex:foo', the exact traced sequence is..."), not shape claims, and only a real assert_eq! against real parse()/next_token() output can confirm or refute them. Applied this project's own established discipline (verify every specific claim against the actual code, don't assume by analogy, per SPEC-009's own `reasoning` field's citation of SPEC-006 AC-004/SPEC-007 AC-014/SPEC-008 AC-010's false-comparative-claim history) one level deeper than the spec itself did: rather than trusting my own first-draft assumption about what "+ +foo" should parse to, I wrote the test, ran it for real, watched it fail against my own assumption, traced why, and corrected the test to match the verified real behavior -- documented in T-009's step text as a worked example of exactly the failure mode this project has repeatedly warned against. Task granularity follows dependency order strictly (Lexer before Modifier/ParsedTerm/parse before QueryPlan, matching the spec's own note that Modifier/ParsedTerm/parse 'likely depend on tokenizing') and keeps every task at a single AC or a tightly related AC pair (AC-010+AC-012 share one task, T-009, because both are proven by the same handful of parse()-level assertions about content_to_term's dispatch -- splitting them would mean re-deriving the identical Lexer/parse setup twice for no discriminating value). AC-006 is the one criterion deliberately covered across two tasks (T-004, T-005) rather than one, purely for the 15-minute size limit -- its 4 concrete traced examples plus the general unterminated-no-backslash case is too much content for one task at this project's own established per-task granularity.
